note.note:
Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Acute diarrhea with vomiting and abdominal pain for 3 days.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: 3 days ago.
  - Diarrhea: Began watery, now very loose; frequency not precisely known; at least 4 episodes today. No blood noted.
  - Vomiting: Unable to keep down liquids or food; last episode ~2 hours prior to consult after breakfast.
  - Fever: Feels “very hot/boiling”; no temperature measured.
  - Abdominal pain: Periumbilical (around the navel), very tender to touch; intermittent; associated with urge to defecate.
  - Urination: Passing urine; last void ~1 hour prior; urine color not assessed. No hematuria.
  - Rash: None.
  - Baseline bowel habit: Once daily, normal; no prior similar episodes.
  - Exposure: Close contact with brother who has similar symptoms; reports others at his school are ill. No recent travel abroad.
- Past medical history: No chronic conditions reported. Menstrual cramps historically.
- Past surgical history: None reported.
- Medications:
  - Vitamin D taken daily; dose and route not documented.
  - Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Oral rehydration salts (ORS) self-administered ~3 times/day for past 2 days.
- Social history:
  - Occupation: Graphic designer; worked from home today due to illness.
  - Lives with brother and mother.
  - Tobacco: Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: Occasional (a pint from time to time).
  - Recreational drugs: None.
  - Sexual history: Not currently having regular sexual intercourse. Not on contraception. Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- Telemedicine visit; no in-person physical examination performed.
- Vitals: Not recorded. Subjective fever reported.
- Hydration status: Patient reports ongoing urination; last urination ~1 hour prior.
- Investigations: None completed during visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhea with vomiting:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Suspected infectious gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral gastroenteritis; bacterial gastrointestinal infection (foodborne).
   - Investigations planned: Urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool sample analysis to evaluate for bacterial infection.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue oral rehydration salts in very small, frequent sips.
     - Simple diet as tolerated (e.g., toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk temporarily.
     - No antibiotics prescribed at this time.
   - Relevant referrals: Urgent in-clinic assessment arranged. Advise urgent evaluation in the emergency department if clinical status worsens.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergy status; comprehensive past medical/surgical history; full medication reconciliation (doses/routes/frequencies); vitals; physical exam; exact stool frequency and urine color; objective temperature; documentation of weight for dehydration risk.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Generally understandable; some pauses/inaudible or incomplete responses; exact stool frequency not clearly quantified.
